name: manual_5b8341
claim: Run npm from a directory with no package.json and npm roots the install at the nearest ancestor that has a package.json or node_modules, which can be a home-directory project, and it will prune that project's undeclared packages. Always pass an explicit --prefix for a one-off tool install, for example npm install --prefix <repo> --no-save --no-package-lock --ignore-scripts markdownlint-cli2@0.17.2. CI works without the flag only because its checkout has no ancestor project. The lint-gate tests need that exact CI version installed inside the repo (a bare npx cache is not enough).
conditions: npm prefix ancestor package-json markdownlint-cli2 ci-parity

decisions.notes: 2026-11-17: a bare npm install from a repo worktree acted on the home project, left 88 packages renamed aside and failed with ENOTEMPTY; the same command with --prefix installed 0.17.2 in the repo and all 4 gate tests passed. A restore script was prepared and the operator was told.
